# APPENDIX E

## The Agent Registry: Working Template

*Cross-reference: Chapter 14 (The Three Lines and the Trust Boundary), “The Agent Registry” H2 \| Coordinates with Appendix D (Assumption Register), Appendix F (FRIA), Appendix I (Audit Checklist Section 0 Pre-Audit Scoping: Inventory and Actor Classification) and Appendix J Part 6 model card minimums*

| **Registry Version**                                                    |                                                                                                                  |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

## How to Use This Template

You cannot govern what you have not named. The Agent Registry is the centralized inventory of every AI system the organization has deployed, is piloting or has authorized for development, including AI features embedded in commercial software, AI systems deployed by individual business units without central IT involvement and AI agents operating as components of larger orchestrated systems. The structural response to shadow AI is not awareness training. It is registration as a precondition for use.

Each entry contains the information needed to govern the system: purpose and intended use; EU AI Act actor designation and risk classification; internal impact classification; named system owner; oversight mode; trust boundary specification by reference; evidence retention policy; and date of last governance review. The Registry is not a one-time document. It is a living record. A system that was registered as minimal risk and has since been deployed in a regulated sector context is no longer a minimal risk system regardless of what the Registry says; the mechanism owner who fails to update the Registry has created a governance gap through which the system operates outside the controls that would apply if its actual deployment context were known.

For each entry: complete all fields. Do not leave fields blank. Where a field is not applicable, state the basis for non-applicability. The Registry is reviewed for completeness by a named mechanism owner at defined intervals (quarterly is the minimum default; faster cadence required for high-impact systems and for organizations in active scaling). New entries require approval at the level appropriate to the system’s impact classification before the system reaches production.

This template is synchronized with Appendix I Section 0 (Pre-Audit Scoping: Inventory and Actor Classification). Where an audit checklist question can be answered by reference to a Registry field, cross-reference rather than restate; the Registry is the system of record for system inventory.

## Field Schema

| **Section E │ Per-System Fields** *One row per AI system in the organization. Fields E1-E17 are mandatory. New rows added as systems are registered; entries for Retired systems are retained for audit.*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Field**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **E1 Registry ID** Unique identifier for the system within the Registry. Once issued, never reassigned even after the system is Retired. Format must support cross-reference from FRIA, Assumption Register, audit checklist responses and incident reports.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **E2 System Name, Version and Vendor / Origin** System name as it appears in operational documentation; deployed version (model identifier and build); origin classification (in-house developed; commercial off-the-shelf; commercial with deployment-specific configuration; open-source with internal modification; vendor-provided embedded feature in third-party software). Embedded AI features in commercial software are in scope; their omission is the most common Registry gap.                                                                                     |
| **E3 System Purpose and Intended Use** The specific purpose for which the system is deployed in the organization. If narrower than the vendor’s stated intended use, record the delta and the basis for the narrower scope. Cross-reference to Appendix F Field A1 where a FRIA exists; otherwise state the purpose here.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **E4 EU AI Act Actor Designation** Provider (Art. 3(3)), Deployer (Art. 3(4)), Authorized Representative (Art. 3(5)), Importer (Art. 3(6)), Distributor (Art. 3(7)), Product Manufacturer (Art. 3(8)), Multiple roles or Other (not an AI Act operator role). Record the basis. A deployer, distributor, importer or other third party becomes the provider of a high-risk AI system under Art. 25(1) if it (a) puts its name or trademark on a high-risk system, (b) substantially modifies a high-risk system that remains high-risk or (c) modifies the intended purpose of a system that is not high-risk so that it becomes high-risk; the basis recorded here is the determination that resolves that question for the current deployment. Re-assess on every material change.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **E5 EU AI Act Risk Classification** Prohibited (Art. 5); High-Risk (Annex I via Art. 6(1), or Annex III via Art. 6(2), subject to Art. 6(3)); Limited-Risk (Art. 50 transparency obligations apply); Minimal Risk; General-Purpose AI Model with or without Systemic Risk; Other or Not Applicable (with basis). Where Limited-Risk, record the specific Art. 50 obligation and the deployer or provider responsibility for it.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **E6 Internal Impact Classification** Organization-defined classification, distinct from the regulatory classification. A system classified Minimal Risk under the AI Act may still be Tier-1 internally because it operates in a politically sensitive context, supports a fiduciary duty or affects employee outcomes. Internal classification governs internal control intensity; regulatory classification governs the statutory obligations. Both are recorded.                                                                                                            |
| **E7 Assigned System Owner** The accountable executive named for this deployment, who carries Final Liability for it under the allocation of Chapter 7. Not a function title. Not a department. A specific person with decision rights over the deployment, oversight of it and the power to intervene, including the standing to halt the system if the trust boundary is breached. Record beside the owner the supporting roles the allocation assigns, each individually identified with its domain: authority design (General Counsel), enforcement and evidence (engineering) and assurance (internal audit). Supporting roles do not share Final Liability.                                                                                                        |
| **E8 Oversight Mode and Rationale** Human-in-the-Loop, Human-on-the-Loop or Human-in-Command. Recorded with the rationale for the mode chosen given the system’s impact classification. Any reduction of oversight mode (HITL to HOTL, HOTL to HIC) is a governance event requiring formal approval at the appropriate level; the approval record is referenced here.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **E9 Trust Boundary Specification Reference** Reference to the document in which the authorized zone, escalation zone and prohibited zone are specified for this system. The Registry does not duplicate the specification; it points to it. The specification document itself is version-controlled and reviewed at the cadence stated in E14.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **E10 Data Sources and Downstream Systems** Inputs (data sources, upstream systems, retrieval indexes, tools the agent may call); outputs (downstream systems the agent may write to, third-party services it may transact with, communication channels it may use). Material change to either side is a governance event requiring re-assessment under E4 and E11.                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **E11 FRIA Status** Required (Art. 27 applicability triggered) and Reference; Required and Pending (with target completion date and basis for pre-FRIA operation if any); Not Required (with basis under Art. 27(1) applicability test). For systems where FRIA is Not Required but internal impact classification is Tier-1 or Tier-2, an internal rights-and-impact assessment may still be required by organizational policy; record the reference.                                                                                                                          |
| **E12 Evidence Retention Policy** What logs are kept (action logs, prompt and output logs, escalation records, human review documentation, model and configuration version history, monitoring metric history); for how long (retention period with regulatory and contractual basis); who has access (roles authorized to read, roles authorized to extract for audit, roles authorized to modify the retention configuration); tamper-evidence mechanism; access-event logging. Retrofitted evidence is not evidence of governance.                                           |
| **E13 Vendor and Supply Chain References** Vendor name and entity; contract reference and term; change-notification clause reference; audit-rights clause reference; sub-processor and sub-model dependencies; vendor governance assessment date and outcome (cross-reference to Appendix I, Checklist IDs 1.17 to 1.19). Concentration risk flag where this vendor or model also supports other Tier-1 or Tier-2 systems in the Registry.                                                                                                                                                 |
| **E14 Date of Last Governance Review and Next Scheduled Review** Date of last review and named reviewer. Next scheduled review date, with cadence proportionate to impact classification (Tier-1: quarterly minimum; Tier-2: semi-annual minimum; Tier-3: annual). Trigger events that bring the next review forward are recorded in this field.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **E15 Status** Pilot (limited population, contained operating envelope, documented exit criteria); Production (full operating envelope, full evidence pipeline active); Production-Restricted (production but with active conditions on continued deployment from a FRIA Section H or Assumption Register Falsification response); Suspended (operations halted pending resolution of an identified issue, with reference); Retired (no longer in use; entry retained for audit). Pilot-to-Production promotion is a governance event; the promotion record is referenced here. |
| **E16 Change History** Versioned record of material changes to the system’s registered configuration: version upgrades; permission changes; new data sources; integration changes; oversight mode changes; impact-classification changes; ownership changes; status changes. Entries are not deleted. The Change History is the audit trail that demonstrates the Registry operated as a control rather than as a static inventory.                                                                                                                                             |
| **E17 Enforcement Points and Stop Test** For each condition in the trust boundary (E9), where it is enforced: outside the model (system architecture or configuration), by credential scope, at a human gate or by instruction to the model only. A condition enforced by instruction only is recorded as such and reported to the system owner (E7), because an instruction the model can ignore is not a boundary. Record the last stop test: the date pause and rollback were last exercised and the measured time from the decision to stop to the system stopping (Chapter 22, Question 51). |

## Worked Example

| **Worked Example │ Agent Registry Entry** *Illustrative entry for an agentic customer-service triage system*                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Field**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **E1 Registry ID** AGR-CS-007                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **E2 System Name, Version and Vendor / Origin** CustomerTriage Assistant v3.2.1 (vendor: ExampleAI Ltd; commercial off-the-shelf with deployment-specific configuration; underlying model: ExampleAI-Large v2.4 (vendor release 1 February 2026; deployed here 1 April 2026); retrieval index: internal complaints knowledge base v2026.04).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **E3 System Purpose and Intended Use** Triage of inbound customer complaints into routing categories (general, financial regulated, discrimination regulated, safety regulated, other regulated) and assignment of priority level. Where a complainant who is a natural person applies for hardship credit or forbearance, the triage output also scores the application and is an input to the lender’s evaluation of that person’s creditworthiness. Narrower than vendor intended use, which includes drafting initial response text; that capability is disabled in deployment configuration. Delta basis: rights-impact assessment determined that response drafting at the triage layer creates an unacceptable risk of premature settlement language reaching the customer record.                                                                                                  |
| **E4 EU AI Act Actor Designation** Deployer. No Art. 25(1) trigger applies: the system carries the vendor’s name, the model is not substantially modified and the deployment configuration narrows rather than changes the intended purpose. Re-assessment on next vendor model upgrade.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **E5 EU AI Act Risk Classification** High-Risk. Annex III point 5(b) basis (evaluation of the creditworthiness of natural persons: the hardship-credit and forbearance scoring described in E3 is an input to that evaluation; complaint triage as such is not within point 5(b)). Provider Art. 16 obligations carried by ExampleAI Ltd; deployer Art. 26 obligations carried by us. Art. 27 FRIA required from 2 December 2027 and completed in advance (Reference: FRIA-2026-014, dated 28 March 2026).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| **E6 Internal Impact Classification** Tier-1. High volume; affects customer access to remedy; regulator interest in complaints handling sector-wide.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **E7 Assigned System Owner** Jane Doe, Director of Customer Operations, accountable executive for this deployment. Supporting roles: authority design, Office of the General Counsel; enforcement and evidence pipeline, Raj Patel, Head of AI Platform Engineering; assurance, Internal Audit.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| **E8 Oversight Mode and Rationale** HOTL on general routing decisions; HITL on regulated-harm categories (financial, discrimination, safety) before any customer-facing action. Rationale: rights-impact analysis in FRIA-2026-014 (draft v0.3 of 10 March 2026, Sections D and E; final issued 28 March 2026) determined that regulated-harm mis-routing exceeds tolerable residual risk without per-decision human review. Approval: Executive Risk Committee 12 March 2026.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **E9 Trust Boundary Specification Reference** Trust Boundary Specification CTA-TBS-v1.4 dated 18 March 2026 (current). Authorized zone: routing among general categories and assigning standard priority. Escalation zone: any complaint scoring above threshold on any regulated-harm classifier; any complaint with named identifiers consistent with vulnerable categories. Prohibited zone: composing customer-facing text; closing complaint records; modifying ground-truth labels in the QA dataset.                                                                                                                                                            |
| **E10 Data Sources and Downstream Systems** Inputs: inbound complaint text channel (email, web form, transcribed voice); customer record system read-only API; complaints knowledge base. Outputs: case management system (write: routing category, priority level, classifier confidence vector); credit decisioning system (write: hardship-credit and forbearance application score); QA dashboard (write: per-decision metadata for sampling). No third-party services. No outbound communication channels.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **E11 FRIA Status** Required and Reference: FRIA-2026-014 dated 28 March 2026, next scheduled review 28 March 2027 or on material change.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| **E12 Evidence Retention Policy** Action logs (every triage decision, classifier output vector, model and configuration version, timestamp, outcome): 7 years (sector retention requirement). Escalation records: 7 years. Human review documentation for HITL decisions: 7 years. Monitoring metric history: 5 years. Tamper evidence: write-once storage with cryptographic chain. Access: read by the governance, risk management and compliance function, Internal Audit and Legal; extract by Internal Audit and Legal; modify retention configuration requires dual control (System Owner plus Head of Governance, Risk Management and Compliance).                                                                                                            |
| **E13 Vendor and Supply Chain References** ExampleAI Ltd, Master Services Agreement dated 4 January 2026, term 36 months. Change-notification clause Schedule 2 Clause 3.4 (30 days advance written notice for any material model change). Audit-rights clause Schedule 2 Clause 7.1 (annual on-site, additional on serious incident). Sub-processor: ExampleAI Cloud Hosting LLC (US); model dependency: ExampleAI-Large v2.4. Vendor governance assessment dated 18 February 2026 (of the vendor and of v2.3, before the upgrade), outcome Pass-with-Conditions, conditions tracked in Appendix I responses to Checklist IDs 1.17 to 1.19. Concentration flag: Yes; vendor also supports AGR-FIN-003 (Tier-2) and AGR-HR-009 (Tier-2). |
| **E14 Date of Last Governance Review and Next Scheduled Review** Last review 22 April 2026 (Jane Doe and Raj Patel). Next scheduled review 22 July 2026 (quarterly cadence per Tier-1 default). Trigger-forward conditions: any vendor model upgrade; any change in regulated-harm classifier performance triggering Assumption Register ASR-2026-014 falsification; any escalation rate change exceeding 25 percent week-over-week.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **E15 Status** Production. Promoted from Pilot 1 March 2026 (promotion record: Executive Risk Committee minutes 26 February 2026).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **E16 Change History** v1.0 entry created 12 January 2026 (Pilot status). v1.1 trust boundary tightened to disable response drafting 5 February 2026. v1.2 promotion to Production 1 March 2026. v1.3 oversight mode split (HOTL general, HITL regulated-harm) 12 March 2026. v1.4 vendor model upgrade ExampleAI-Large v2.3 to v2.4 1 April 2026; Art. 25 reassessment confirmed deployer-only status retained.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **E17 Enforcement Points and Stop Test** Prohibited zone: composing customer-facing text, enforced outside the model (drafting disabled in the deployment configuration, v1.1); closing complaint records and modifying ground-truth labels, enforced by credential scope (the service account has read-only access to case status and to the QA dataset). Escalation zone: enforced at a human gate (HITL queue). No condition rests on instruction to the model only. Stop test: pause and rollback exercised 15 April 2026; measured time from decision to stop 4 minutes against a target of 10. |

**Final Liability rests with the Human.**
